What is software architecture?
Software architecture is the high-level structure of a software system, defining its components, their responsibilities, and how they interact to meet functional and quality requirements.
You are an expert in software architecture, algorithms, and performance, you are here to help others.
What is a monolithic architecture?
A monolithic architecture is one where the entire application is built and deployed as a single, unified unit, with all components tightly bound together in one codebase.

What is a microservices architecture?
A microservices architecture structures an application as a collection of small, independent services that communicate over a network, each responsible for a specific business capability.

What is the difference between monolithic and microservices architecture?

A monolith is deployed as one unit and is simpler to start with, while microservices split functionality into independently deployable services that scale and evolve separately but add operational complexity.

What is the MVC pattern?

MVC (Model-View-Controller) is an architectural pattern that separates an application into the model (data and logic), the view (user interface), and the controller (which handles input and coordinates the two).

What is the MVVM pattern?
MVVM (Model-View-ViewModel) separates the UI (view) from business logic (model) using a view model that exposes data and commands, enabling data binding and easier testing.

What is a design pattern?
A design pattern is a reusable, proven solution to a commonly occurring problem in software design, such as the Singleton, Observer, or Factory pattern.

What is the Singleton pattern?
The Singleton pattern ensures a class has only one instance and provides a single global point of access to it, often used for shared resources like configuration or logging.

What is the Observer pattern?
The Observer pattern defines a one-to-many relationship where multiple observer objects are automatically notified when the state of a subject object changes.

What is separation of concerns?
Separation of concerns is a design principle that divides a system into distinct parts, each handling a specific responsibility, making the system easier to understand, maintain, and modify.

What is a layered architecture?
A layered architecture organizes a system into horizontal layers such as presentation, business logic, and data access, where each layer communicates only with the layer directly below it.

What is client-server architecture?
Client-server architecture splits a system into clients that request services and a server that provides them, communicating over a network.

What is an API gateway?
An API gateway is a single entry point that sits in front of backend services, handling routing, authentication, rate limiting, and request aggregation, commonly used in microservices.

What is event-driven architecture?
Event-driven architecture is a design where components communicate by producing and reacting to events, enabling loose coupling and asynchronous processing.

What is a load balancer?
A load balancer distributes incoming network traffic across multiple servers to improve availability, reliability, and performance by preventing any single server from being overwhelmed.

What is the difference between horizontal and vertical scaling?
Horizontal scaling adds more machines to handle load, while vertical scaling adds more resources (CPU, memory) to an existing machine.

What are coupling and cohesion?
Coupling measures how dependent modules are on each other, while cohesion measures how focused a module's responsibilities are; good design favors low coupling and high cohesion.

What is dependency injection?
Dependency injection is a technique where an object receives its dependencies from an external source rather than creating them itself, improving modularity and testability.

What is serverless architecture?
Serverless architecture lets developers run code in response to events without managing servers, with the cloud provider handling provisioning and scaling automatically.

What is caching in software architecture?
Caching stores frequently accessed data in a fast-access layer so future requests can be served quickly, reducing load on databases and improving response times.

What is a message queue?
A message queue is a component that lets services communicate asynchronously by sending messages that are stored until the receiving service processes them, improving decoupling and resilience.

What is the difference between synchronous and asynchronous communication?
In synchronous communication the caller waits for a response before continuing, while in asynchronous communication the caller continues without waiting and is notified later.

What is an algorithm?
An algorithm is a finite, well-defined sequence of steps designed to solve a specific problem or perform a computation.

What is time complexity?
Time complexity describes how the running time of an algorithm grows relative to the size of its input, usually expressed with Big O notation.

What is Big O notation?
Big O notation describes the upper bound of an algorithm's growth rate, expressing how its time or space requirements scale as input size increases.

What is space complexity?
Space complexity describes how much memory an algorithm needs relative to the size of its input.

What is the difference between O(n) and O(n^2)?
O(n) means runtime grows linearly with input size, while O(n^2) means it grows quadratically, becoming much slower as the input gets large.

What is a sorting algorithm?
A sorting algorithm arranges the elements of a list into a specific order, such as ascending or descending; examples include quicksort, merge sort, and bubble sort.

What is binary search?
Binary search is an efficient algorithm for finding a value in a sorted array by repeatedly dividing the search range in half, running in O(log n) time.

What is a recursive algorithm?
A recursive algorithm solves a problem by calling itself on smaller subproblems until it reaches a base case that can be solved directly.

What is a greedy algorithm?
A greedy algorithm makes the locally optimal choice at each step, hoping to reach a globally optimal solution; it works well for some problems but not all.

What is dynamic programming?
Dynamic programming solves complex problems by breaking them into overlapping subproblems and storing their results to avoid recomputation.

What is a hash table?
A hash table is a data structure that maps keys to values using a hash function, allowing average constant-time lookups, insertions, and deletions.

What is a linked list?
A linked list is a linear data structure where each element (node) stores data and a reference to the next node, allowing efficient insertions and deletions.

What is the difference between a stack and a queue?
A stack follows Last-In-First-Out (LIFO) order, while a queue follows First-In-First-Out (FIFO) order.

What is a binary tree?
A binary tree is a hierarchical data structure in which each node has at most two children, commonly referred to as the left and right child.

What is a graph in algorithms?
A graph is a data structure consisting of nodes (vertices) connected by edges, used to represent relationships such as networks, maps, or dependencies.

What is the difference between BFS and DFS?
Breadth-First Search (BFS) explores a graph level by level, while Depth-First Search (DFS) explores as far as possible along each branch before backtracking.

What is the difference between best, average, and worst case complexity?
They describe an algorithm's performance under the most favorable, typical, and least favorable inputs respectively, giving a fuller picture than a single measure.

What is performance optimization?
Performance optimization is the process of improving a system's speed, responsiveness, and resource efficiency by identifying and removing bottlenecks.

What is latency?
Latency is the time it takes for a single request to travel from the source to the destination and receive a response, often measured in milliseconds.

What is throughput?
Throughput is the amount of work or number of requests a system can handle in a given period of time.

What is a memory leak?
A memory leak occurs when a program allocates memory but fails to release it after use, causing memory usage to grow over time and potentially degrade performance.

What is lazy loading?
Lazy loading is a technique that delays loading resources or data until they are actually needed, reducing initial load time and saving resources.

What is profiling in performance analysis?
Profiling is the practice of measuring where a program spends its time and resources, helping developers locate performance bottlenecks.

What is the difference between concurrency and parallelism?
Concurrency is about handling multiple tasks by interleaving their progress, while parallelism is about executing multiple tasks literally at the same time on multiple cores.

How does caching improve performance?
Caching improves performance by storing the results of expensive operations or frequently used data so they can be reused quickly instead of recomputed or refetched.
